content.jointProblem: How can a Serbian Cyrillic–Latin transliteration and normalization layer be placed in a PostgreSQL full-text-search pipeline — at index time, at query time, or both — so that mixed-script contract documents return correct hits without noticeably increasing response times?

rationale.text: Has a directly relevant Cyrillic–Latin normalisation and diacritic-robust comparison method for Serbian data.

sources.quote: incorporating a rule-based Cyrillic–Latin normaliser, a diacritic-robust string distance metric derived from Jaro–Winkler

rationale.text: Works with PostgreSQL and Python-based matching frameworks, matching the company stack.

sources.quote: The group works with PostgreSQL, Python-based matching frameworks, and RDF triple stores

rationale.text: Has led schema harmonisation and ontology-construction work in a cross-platform data-linkage project.

sources.quote: Slađana Ranković led the work package on schema harmonisation and ontology construction

rationale.text: Has applied industry consultancy experience integrating legacy system exports with an ERP platform.

sources.quote: provided consultancy to a regional logistics company during 2020–2021 on the integration of legacy warehouse management system exports with a new ERP platform

rationale.text: Is open to joint research projects and contract research on data integration and data quality assessment.

sources.quote: contract research on data integration and data quality assessment

risks: The Cyrillic–Latin normaliser was evaluated on voter-registration record pairs, not on PostgreSQL full-text search over contract documents; transfer to this task is unproven and should be the first experiment.
Dialect conventions create ambiguous transliteration cases that a rule-based normaliser may not resolve without a policy.
The six-week, one-engineer company capacity may be too short for robust mixed-script handling plus latency benchmarking.
Researcher availability is unknown and notes indicate moderate capacity, so scheduling and scope may fail.
No evidence in the researcher material shows prior implementation of transliteration inside PostgreSQL FTS or performance tuning for search latency.
Contract document access and anonymization for testing are not specified.
